intended_object: A step inside a proof. It builds the sheaf-level part of the universal lift into a candidate limit cone C of sheafed spaces from a competing cone Q. It comes from the docstring, the module doc ("an actual cone is limiting if its base cone is limiting and the cocone of inverse-image sheaves is colimiting") and its use in `conePullbackLimitLift`.
explanation: The definition builds the morphism f^*(C.pt.sheaf) ⟶ Q.pt.sheaf. Here f is the map of base spaces given by the limit property of the underlying topological cone. The morphism comes from the universal property of the colimiting cocone `hsheaf`, after pulling it back along f (pullback of sheaves is a left adjoint, so it preserves colimits). The cocone it maps to is `conePullbackLimitTargetCocone`. The definition takes proof data as hypotheses (`hbase`, `hsheaf`), and the only places it is used are `conePullbackLimitSheafMap_fac` and the construction of `conePullbackLimitLift`. Those in turn prove that C is a limit cone in `SheafedSpace A`. It is therefore an intermediate piece of a limit-detection argument, not a standalone notion from the literature, so there is nothing to compare it against. It does what its docstring says.
